chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated:

I sent dinars to al-Riḍā عليه السلام on behalf of some of my family, and I wrote to him informing him that among them there was zakat, seventy-five, and the remainder was a gift. So he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received [it].”
And I sent to him dinars for myself and for others, and I wrote to him that they were from the fiṭrah of the dependants, so he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received [it].”

key_terms.زَكَاةً: zakat, the obligatory alms due from wealth
key_terms.صِلَةٌ: a gift or offering sent as a gesture of connection
key_terms.فِطْرَةِ: fiṭrah alms given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام acknowledge receiving zakat and fiṭrah sent to him?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ sending zakat and fiṭrah funds to al-Riḍā عليه السلام, including amounts on behalf of family members and others. The Imam’s written acknowledgement of receipt shows the delivery and acceptance of these charitable dues.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1640 - Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi’ narrated:

I sent some dinars to al-Ridha (Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (as)) on behalf of some of my family members. I wrote to him informing him that seventy-five of them were Zakat, and the remainder was a gift.
Imam (as) wrote back in his handwriting: "I have received them."
